new_public_evidence.source: Lee and Whiteley, Variance estimation in the particle filter
new_public_evidence.result: Single-run genealogy variance estimation and time-step decomposition remain the allocation benchmark, but its finite-N genealogy guarantees are not imported unchanged into independent stratified resampling.

new_public_evidence.source: Mastrototaro and Olsson, Adaptive online variance estimation in particle filters: the ALVar estimator
new_public_evidence.result: Lag-adaptive ancestry grouping motivates the new coalescence-increment diagnostic as a localizer; this run does not claim the heuristic is the ALVar estimator or theorem-equivalent under stratified resampling.

new_public_evidence.source: Flenghi and Jourdain, Central limit theorem for the stratified resampling mechanism
new_public_evidence.result: The direct stratified-resampling CLT is rigorous, while the later-step particle-filter variance recursion is presented under a conjectured convergence property; the desired theorem-clean single-run generation-wise estimator remains open in the searched sources.

new_public_evidence.source: Li, Wang, Deng and Liu, Stratification and Optimal Resampling for Sequential Monte Carlo
new_public_evidence.result: Supports stratified/ordered resampling as a variance-reduction mechanism, but not as a single-run variance-estimator theorem.

new_public_evidence.source: Koskela, Jenkins, Johansen and Spano, Genealogical processes of sequential Monte Carlo methods and other non-neutral population models under rapid mutation
new_public_evidence.result: Recent genealogy theory reinforces that genealogy depends materially on the resampling mechanism; used only as background for keeping multinomial and stratified genealogy claims separate.

derived_results.claim: In a 12-generation two-state Feynman-Kac model with a single moving shock and independent stratified resampling, the completed-run continuation-value CV^2 proxy tracked exact generation coefficients very closely across shock positions 0..10: mean correlation 0.99867, minimum 0.99659, mean normalized-share L1 error 0.03038, and dominant generation 11/11. A lag-4 coalescence-increment genealogy heuristic also localized the dominant generation 11/11 but had mean correlation 0.90130 and mean normalized-share L1 error 0.29148. The terminal generation is structurally blind to this pure descendant-coalescence diagnostic.

For a fixed allocation q, the asymptotic variance ratio to uniform is a weighted average of r_p=1/(T q_p). Over coordinate box L<=A<=U, the exact maximum is obtained by a threshold assignment that places U on coordinates with r_p above the maximizing ratio and L below it. A sorted threshold scan therefore computes the exact conditional box inflation cap without enumerating 2^T corners.

Using a past-only rolling uncertainty box, EWMA 0.6, beta grid {0,.25,.5,.65,.75,.85,.9}, and conditional box cap 1.30, 40-stream exact schedule scoring gave mean asymptotic variance ratios to uniform of 0.85444 abrupt, 0.81535 gradual and 0.86431 recurring, corresponding to 14.56%, 18.47% and 13.57% reductions. Mean beta was 0.872/0.900/0.781. Worst single-run ratios were 1.184, 1.000 and 1.266. Empirical true-coefficient box coverage was only 0.907, 0.704 and 0.848, so the 1.30 cap is explicitly conditional rather than unconditional.

Driving the same uncertainty allocation directly from the lagged genealogy coalescence increment gave weaker mean exact ratios 0.92356/0.90275/0.91461 and empirical true-coefficient box coverage only 0.0050/0.0054/0.0022 in abrupt/gradual/recurring stress. Despite good dominant-generation localization, its magnitude is not calibrated to A, so it should be used as a drift/localization channel rather than as the coefficient vector inside a variance cap.

The older fixed beta=0.5 continuation controller had smaller average gains but much smaller stale transients: mean exact ratios 0.89203/0.86294/0.88111 and worst single-run ratios 1.0607/1.0000/1.0715. Aggressive uncertainty-aware concentration therefore improves average efficiency at the price of larger transient risk when the uncertainty set undercovers drift.

Because all compared schedules spend the same 768-particle variable budget and share the same fixed per-run overhead, the r124 confirmation-latency algebra makes the exact asymptotic variance ratios equal the idealized equal-cost confirmation-latency ratios. The continuation uncertainty controller therefore implies model-specific idealized latency reductions of about 14.6%, 18.5% and 13.6% under abrupt, gradual and recurring stress respectively.

A fresh targeted public-source search did not locate a theorem-clean single-run generation-wise variance estimator for a multi-generation particle filter with independent stratified resampling. This is not a nonexistence claim. The closest direct stratified CLT source still leaves the later-step recursive particle-filter formula conditional on a conjecture.

engineering_update.scope: Twelve-generation synthetic two-state Feynman-Kac stress with independent stratified resampling. Exact schedule scoring uses true model coefficients only post hoc; online schedules use completed-run diagnostics. Numeric gains are model-specific.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The genealogy coalescence increment is not coefficient-calibrated even when it correctly identifies the dominant generation; its uncertainty box cannot support a variance-inflation guarantee.

The continuation uncertainty box is heuristic and undercovered smooth drift in this stress, reaching only about 70% empirical coverage in the gradual scenario; the nominal 1.30 cap is conditional on box coverage.
Aggressive beta produced transient exact variance ratios up to about 1.27 under recurring drift; fixed beta=0.5 was less efficient on average but limited tested transients to about 1.07.
The terminal generation cannot be identified by descendant coalescence because it has no following resampling step.
No multinomial genealogy theorem was transferred to the stratified implementation, and no theorem-clean stratified single-run generation-wise estimator was established.
Finite-particle normalized-MSE validation was smaller and noisier than exact schedule scoring; exact asymptotic schedule ratios are the primary quantitative comparison.
No AGI capability or real-agent performance claim follows from this synthetic particle model.
frontier: Construct a coverage-calibrated, past-only uncertainty set for normalized continuation/influence coefficients under dependent stratified particles; until then keep any beta cap explicitly conditional.

Use the genealogy coalescence increment only as a drift detector/localizer. When its dominant generation changes or it strongly disagrees with the continuation center, predictably inflate the continuation uncertainty set or temporarily clamp beta; tune on discovery seeds and validate once on disjoint streams.

Continue targeted public-source search for a rigorous single-run generation-wise variance estimator under independent stratified multi-generation SMC; otherwise keep theorem and heuristic layers separate.
Extend to 20 generations and add a terminal boundary diagnostic based on local weight/influence variation.
Extend equal-cost allocation to predictable random per-generation tool costs and parallel descendants, optimizing confirmation latency using only completed-run influence and cost estimates.
exact_next_action: Keep continuation CV^2 as the coefficient estimator and treat lagged genealogy only as a change alarm. Build a past-only alarmed controller that widens the continuation coefficient box and clamps beta for a fixed cooldown when genealogy changes generation or materially disagrees with continuation. Tune alarm/cooldown on one discovery seed family, freeze it, then validate on disjoint abrupt/gradual/recurring streams using exact schedule ratio, finite normalized MSE, empirical box coverage, worst transient ratio and adaptation lag. In parallel search for confidence-sequence or conservative set methods for normalized influence coefficients under dependent stratified clouds and continue the theorem search for stratified single-run genealogy variance estimation.
